dishes.name: Salmon Teriyaki
dishes.description: Glossy soy-and-mirin salmon, fluffy short-grain rice and crisp green vegetables. A little Japanese comfort for your dinner table.
steps: Cook the rice
Rinse the rice until the water is mostly clear. Add the measured rice water, or follow your rice cooker’s guidance for the rice you use. Cook, then let it stand covered for 10 minutes.
Mix the teriyaki sauce
Stir together soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar. Pat the salmon dry and check for pin bones. Thinly slice the scallion.
Cook the vegetables
Steam the broccolini or green beans for 3–5 minutes until bright and tender. Set aside while you cook the fish.
Sear and glaze the salmon

Heat the oil over medium heat. Place the salmon skin-side down for about 4–5 minutes, turn and cook the other side. Add the sauce and simmer gently, spooning it over the fish. Check the thickest part reaches 63°C / 145°F.
Bring it to the table
Serve the glazed salmon with rice and vegetables. Spoon over a little reduced sauce and finish with sesame seeds and scallion.
dishes.tip: Reduce the glaze gently: soy sauce can become too salty if boiled down too far.
dishes.safety: Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C / 145°F, checked with a food thermometer. Cooking times vary with the thickness of the food.

dishes.name: Bife de Chorizo
dishes.description: Argentine striploin steak with parsley chimichurri and golden potato wedges. Despite its name, this is a steak, not a sausage.
steps: Roast the potatoes
Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Cut potatoes into wedges and toss with one third of the oil and a little salt. Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender and golden.
Make the chimichurri
Finely chop parsley and garlic. Mix with the remaining olive oil, vinegar, oregano, chili flakes and a little salt. Let it sit while the steak cooks.
Sear the steak

Pat the steak dry and season with the remaining salt and pepper. Heat a heavy pan over medium-high heat. Sear for roughly 3–4 minutes per side; adjust for thickness and reduce the heat if the surface darkens too quickly.
Check and rest
Use a food thermometer: the middle of a whole-cut steak should reach at least 63°C / 145°F. Rest on a clean plate for at least 3 minutes before slicing.
Serve with the herbs
Slice across the grain, spoon chimichurri over the steak and add the potato wedges. Put any extra chimichurri on the table.
dishes.tip: Chop the herbs by hand for a loose, bright chimichurri rather than a smooth puree.
dishes.safety: For whole-cut beef, reach at least 63°C / 145°F and rest for at least 3 minutes before slicing. Use a food thermometer rather than color alone.

dishes.name: Thai Green Curry
dishes.description: Fragrant green curry with chicken, coconut milk, tender eggplant and Thai basil. A home-kitchen version of gaeng khiao wan gai.
steps: Prepare the rice and vegetables
Cook jasmine rice according to its package instructions. Cut eggplant into bite-size pieces, slice the chili and tear the lime leaves. Slice the chicken using a separate board.
Bloom the curry paste
Heat the oil over medium heat. Stir in the green curry paste for about 1 minute until fragrant; lower the heat if it catches.
Build the coconut sauce
Stir in a little coconut milk until the paste loosens, then add the rest along with the stock or water and lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer the chicken and eggplant
Add chicken and eggplant. Simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, until the eggplant is tender and the thickest chicken pieces reach 74°C / 165°F.
Balance and finish
Add fish sauce and sugar a little at a time, tasting as you go because curry pastes vary in saltiness. Stir in Thai basil and chili, remove the lime leaves and serve with rice.
dishes.tip: Start with less curry paste if you are sensitive to heat; you can add more before the chicken goes in.
dishes.safety: Cook chicken to 74°C / 165°F at its thickest point, checked with a food thermometer. Keep raw poultry and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

dishes.name: Chicken Pho
dishes.description: A weeknight take on Vietnam’s pho ga: clear, ginger-scented broth, tender chicken, rice noodles and a generous handful of herbs.
steps: Toast the aromatics
Halve the onion and ginger. Place cut-side down in a dry pan over medium-high heat for a few minutes until lightly charred. Briefly toast star anise and cinnamon until fragrant.
Infuse the broth
Add stock, onion, ginger and spices to a pot. Bring to a simmer and infuse for 10 minutes. This shortcut uses prepared stock rather than a long-simmered bone broth.
Poach the chicken
Add chicken and maintain a gentle simmer for about 12–18 minutes. Check the thickest part reaches 74°C / 165°F, then transfer to a clean plate and shred or slice.
Prepare the noodles
Cook rice noodles according to the packet, drain and divide between warm bowls. Thinly slice scallions and rinse the herbs.
Season and assemble
Strain the broth and season with fish sauce and sugar to taste. Add chicken to the noodles, pour over piping-hot broth, and finish with scallions, herbs and lime wedges.
dishes.tip: A gentle simmer keeps the broth clear. Taste before adding more fish sauce because prepared stocks differ.
dishes.safety: Cook chicken to 74°C / 165°F at its thickest point, checked with a food thermometer. Keep raw poultry and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

dishes.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
dishes.description: A Roman classic of spaghetti, guanciale, Pecorino and black pepper. The silky sauce comes from eggs and pasta water, not cream.
steps: Start the pasta
Bring a pot of water to a boil and add a modest amount of salt. Cook spaghetti until al dente, following its package timing. Reserve the measured pasta water before draining.
Render the guanciale
Cut guanciale into small strips or cubes. Place in a cool skillet, bring to medium heat and cook for about 5–8 minutes until golden and its fat has rendered.
Whisk the egg mixture
In a bowl, whisk pasteurized egg and yolks with Pecorino and most of the black pepper. Add a spoonful of warm pasta water to loosen the mixture.
Toss away from direct heat
Toss drained pasta with guanciale and its fat. Take the pan completely off the heat and wait briefly so it is not sizzling, then add the egg mixture while tossing constantly.
Make it silky
Add reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce is glossy and coats the strands. Serve immediately with remaining pepper and a little extra cheese if desired.
dishes.tip: Keep the pan off direct heat when adding the eggs. A hot, dry pan will scramble the sauce.
dishes.safety: Use pasteurized eggs for this gently heated sauce. Residual pasta heat does not reliably make an ordinary raw egg safe.

dishes.name: Seafood Paella
dishes.description: Saffron-gold rice, shrimp, mussels and sweet pepper, cooked in a wide pan. A seafood paella adapted for a home stovetop.
steps: Prepare the seafood
Clean the shrimp and scrub and debeard the mussels. Discard cracked mussels and any open ones that do not close when tapped. Warm the stock and add saffron.
Build the sofrito
Heat oil in a wide skillet. Soften sliced pepper for 4–5 minutes. Add minced garlic, grated tomato and paprika; cook for 3–4 minutes until the tomato thickens.
Add the rice
Stir in the dry rice for 1 minute. Pour in hot saffron stock, spread the rice into an even layer and bring to a steady simmer. Taste the liquid and adjust salt if needed.
Cook without constant stirring

Simmer for about 10 minutes, then arrange the seafood on top. Cook another 8–12 minutes, adding a little hot water if needed. Seafood should reach 63°C / 145°F; discard mussels that remain closed after cooking.
Rest and serve
When the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed, remove from heat and cover loosely for 5 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges. Avoid scraping the pan if the bottom has burned.
dishes.tip: The rice should simmer in a thin, even layer. Use a wider pan, rather than a deeper pot, when scaling up.
dishes.safety: Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C / 145°F, checked with a food thermometer. Cooking times vary with the thickness of the food.

dishes.name: Butter Chicken
dishes.description: A home-style murgh makhani with tender chicken, spiced tomato sauce, butter and a swirl of cream. Rich, fragrant and gently warming.
steps: Marinate the chicken
Cut chicken into bite-size pieces. Mix with yogurt, half the grated garlic and ginger, half the garam masala, cumin, chili powder and a little salt. Cover and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Prepare the rice
Cook basmati rice according to its packet instructions while the chicken marinates. Keep it covered until serving.
Brown the chicken
Heat half the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Lift chicken from the marinade and brown for 2–3 minutes per side. It will finish cooking in the sauce. Discard leftover raw marinade.
Make the tomato sauce
Add remaining butter, garlic and ginger to a clean section of the pan. Stir briefly, then add tomatoes and remaining garam masala. Simmer for 10 minutes; add a splash of water if too thick.
Finish gently
Return chicken to the sauce and simmer until every piece reaches 74°C / 165°F. Lower the heat and stir in cream and crushed fenugreek. Taste, adjust salt and serve with rice.
dishes.tip: Do not boil hard after adding cream. A longer refrigerated marinade is optional; the stated time includes a short 20-minute marinade.
dishes.safety: Cook chicken to 74°C / 165°F at its thickest point, checked with a food thermometer. Keep raw poultry and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

dishes.name: Ratatouille
dishes.description: A rustic Provençal vegetable stew of eggplant, zucchini, peppers and ripe tomatoes. Simple ingredients, softened slowly into something generous.
steps: Cut the vegetables
Dice eggplant, zucchini, pepper and tomatoes into similar bite-size pieces. Chop onion and garlic. Keep each vegetable separate.
Brown the eggplant
Heat half the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium heat. Brown eggplant for 6–8 minutes, working in batches if necessary. Transfer to a bowl.
Soften the base
Add the remaining oil and soften onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, then zucchini, and cook for another 3–4 minutes.
Simmer slowly
Return eggplant and add tomatoes, thyme, salt and pepper. Cover and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally. Uncover toward the end if the stew is too watery.
Finish with basil
Taste and adjust seasoning. Tear basil over the vegetables and let the pot rest for a few minutes before serving with bread, rice or on its own.
dishes.tip: Browning the eggplant separately adds flavor and keeps the vegetables from collapsing into a puree.

dishes.name: Bibimbap
dishes.description: A colorful rice bowl with separately cooked vegetables, savory beef, gochujang and a fried egg. Mix everything together just before eating.
steps: Cook rice and prepare the toppings
Rinse and cook rice with its measured water, following your rice cooker’s guidance. Julienne carrots, slice mushrooms and mince garlic. Rinse spinach and bean sprouts.
Cook the vegetables separately
Blanch spinach and bean sprouts until tender, drain well and season with a little sesame oil. Sauté carrots and mushrooms separately in small portions of neutral oil.
Cook the beef
Toss beef with soy sauce and garlic. Stir-fry over medium-high heat until cooked through. For whole-cut beef, check 63°C / 145°F and allow at least 3 minutes of rest before serving.
Prepare sauce and eggs
Loosen gochujang with a little water and remaining sesame oil. Fry the eggs in the remaining neutral oil until the whites and yolks are firm.
Arrange, then mix
Divide rice between bowls. Arrange each vegetable and beef in separate sections. Add the eggs, gochujang sauce and sesame seeds. Mix thoroughly at the table so every bite gets a little of everything.
dishes.tip: Cook each topping separately so its flavor and color stay distinct. Add gochujang gradually to control the heat.
dishes.safety: For whole-cut beef, reach at least 63°C / 145°F and rest for at least 3 minutes before slicing. Use a food thermometer rather than color alone. Cook eggs until both whites and yolks are firm.

dishes.name: Chicken Tacos
dishes.description: Soft corn tortillas with lime-marinated chicken, white onion, cilantro and salsa. Bright, simple tacos made for sharing.
steps: Marinate the chicken
Mix the oil, juice from half the limes, minced garlic, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt. Coat chicken and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Reserve the remaining limes for serving.
Prepare the fresh toppings
Finely chop onion and cilantro. Put them in separate bowls with the salsa. Keep this work surface separate from raw chicken preparation.
Sear the chicken

Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Lift chicken from the marinade and cook for about 5–7 minutes per side, adjusting heat for thickness. Check the thickest part reaches 74°C / 165°F. Discard leftover raw marinade.
Rest and warm the tortillas
Rest chicken on a clean board for 3 minutes, then chop into small pieces. Warm corn tortillas briefly on both sides in a dry pan and keep wrapped in a clean towel.
Build your tacos
Fill the warm tortillas with chicken. Add onion, cilantro and salsa, then squeeze lime over each taco. Serve immediately while the tortillas are soft.
dishes.tip: Warm tortillas one at a time and keep them covered; cold corn tortillas are more likely to split.
dishes.safety: Cook chicken to 74°C / 165°F at its thickest point, checked with a food thermometer. Keep raw poultry and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

dishes.name: Horiatiki Salad
dishes.description: Greece’s village salad: ripe tomatoes, cucumber, olives and a generous piece of feta. No lettuce needed—let the vegetables do the talking.
steps: Prepare the vegetables
Wash and dry tomatoes, cucumber and pepper. Cut tomatoes into wedges and cucumber into chunky half-moons. Slice pepper into thin strips.
Slice the onion
Thinly slice the red onion. If you prefer a milder flavor, soak it in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain thoroughly.
Dress lightly
Combine vegetables and olives in a bowl. Add olive oil, vinegar and a small pinch of salt. Toss gently; remember feta and olives will add salt too.
Add the feta
Place the feta on top in one generous piece or a few large chunks. Sprinkle with oregano and spoon a little dressing over it.
Serve straight away
Let the salad stand for 5 minutes so the tomatoes release some juice, then serve. A piece of bread is lovely for the dressing left in the bowl.
dishes.tip: Use the ripest tomatoes you can find, and keep the feta in generous pieces rather than crumbling it finely.

dishes.name: Nasi Goreng
dishes.description: Indonesian fried rice with sweet kecap manis, savory chicken and a fried egg. Cucumber, tomato and crackers bring freshness and crunch.
steps: Prepare cold rice and aromatics
Use rice that was cooled promptly and refrigerated, not rice left at room temperature overnight. Break up clumps. Mince shallots and garlic and dice the chicken on a separate board.
Fry the eggs
Heat a little oil in a skillet. Fry eggs until both whites and yolks are firm, then transfer to a clean plate and keep warm.
Cook the chicken
Add remaining oil and soften shallots and garlic for 1 minute. Add chicken and stir-fry until it reaches 74°C / 165°F in the thickest pieces.
Fry the rice
Add sambal, then rice. Toss over medium-high heat, breaking up clumps. Stir in kecap manis and fish sauce. Reheat the rice thoroughly to 74°C / 165°F, then fold in sliced scallions.
Plate with a fresh finish
Divide fried rice between plates, top with the eggs, and add sliced cucumber, tomato and shrimp crackers. Serve immediately.
dishes.tip: Cold, separate rice grains fry better than freshly cooked wet rice. Scale up by cooking in batches, not by overcrowding the pan.
dishes.safety: Use promptly cooled, refrigerated cooked rice and reheat it to 74°C / 165°F. Cook chicken to 74°C / 165°F and eggs until both whites and yolks are firm.
